questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence ****given**** with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Despite his pleas, she looked ________ his insincere apologies.
questions.solution:
The phrase that we are here referring to is ‘look through somebody or something’. It means to pretend not to notice somebody or something.

The sentence conveys that although he pleaded (begged/requested), she **ignored/pretended to not notice** his insincere apologies.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

__Complete sentence__ - *Despite his pleas, she looked **through** his insincere apologies*

questions.question:
**Fill in the blank with the most suitable word.**

We won an unprecedented pardon from ______ -President Karzai, and Gulnaz was freed.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **Then.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct answer to fill in the blank is** "then."**
 
• The word 'won' should indicate the granting of pardon from the president of the past time.
 
• **Then** means **(at) that time (in the past or in the future)**.
 
 
• Example: I wanted to live in the city, but my **then husband **(= the man who was my husband at that time) preferred the country.
 
 
 
• So "then-President Karzai" means that at the time when this event happened, Karzai was the president. 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

**Correct Sentence**__: *We won an unprecedented pardon from __**then**__-President Karzai, and Gulnaz was freed.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The other options do not fit grammatically or contextually:
 
• "**Those**" is a pronoun that refers to a specific group of people or things. 
 
• **"At time"** is a phrase that does not provide a clear sense of time or indicate a specific point in time. It lacks the specificity required in this sentence.
 
• **"Later"** is an adverb that indicates a subsequent time or a point in the future.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Sir, can you reflect on the usefulness or _______ of blocking all the highways?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 2'** i.e.** 'Futility'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this context, **"futility"** is the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.
 
• **"Futility" **means the pointlessness or uselessness of an action.
 
• This **word is used when** an action doesn't produce any useful results, which complements the word** "usefulness" **in the sentence.
 
• The **speaker is asking for** reflection on whether blocking all the highways is useful or pointless.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *'Sir, can you reflect on the usefulness or **futility **of blocking all the highways?*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's look at the other options:
 
 
• **"Impotence"** generally refers to a lack of power or ability, which doesn't fit the context here.
 
• **"Scorch" **means to burn slightly or to cause discoloration due to heat. It's not appropriate in this context.
 
• **"Incompatibility"** refers to the state of two things being so different in nature that they cannot coexist. It does not fit the context here.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be ﬁlled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Everyone is mad ______ each other.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is-** 'at'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****

__
 
• 
 
**Prepositions of direction** indicate the location of a noun (a person, place, or thing) in relation to another noun.

 
 
• 
 
Prepositions precede a noun or a pronoun and often accompany verbs of motion.

 
 
• 
 
The verb **mad **can be followed by different prepositions depending on the meaning.

 
 
• 
 
**Mad at** means angry with someone or something.

 
 
• 
 
**Mad for **means crazy about someone or something.

 
 
• 
 
**Mad towards** means having a hostile attitude towards someone or something.

 
 
• 
 
**Mad to** means foolish or insane to do something.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
In this sentence, the meaning is that everyone is angry with each other, so the appropriate preposition is **at**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

The other options are incorrect because:

**Option 1** uses **to**, which implies movement or direction towards a destination or goal. It does not fit with the verb mad.

**Option 2** uses **for**, which implies a reason, purpose, or preference. It does not fit with the verb mad.

**Option 3** uses towards, which implies a hostile attitude or intention. It does not fit with the verb mad.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be ﬁlled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

She does not agree, and ______ does Anita.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'neither'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• ***'Neither' ***as an **adverb**, is used to introduce a further negative statement, e.g., **"He didn't remember, and neither did I" **
 
• ***'Also' ***means *'in addition to'*. Using '**also' **here is grammatically incorrect as it is not negative in nature
 
• *'Even' *means *'including...'*. Using 'even' here is grammatically incorrect as it is not negative in nature
 
• ***'So' ***means *'thus, as a result,...'*. Using 'so' here is grammatically incorrect as it is not negative in nature and in fact, tends to give contradictory meaning

 

**Complete Sentence: ***She does not agree, and **neither **does Anita.*

questions.question:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e. **descended**.

declined- (typically of something regarded as good) become smaller, fewer, or less; decrease.

descended- move or fall downwards.

collapsed- (of a structure) suddenly fall down or give way.

grounded- well balanced and sensible.

Option 2 is contextually fits the sentence and gives a proper meaning.
